Quick findings from logs (first-pass):
- Error surface: ~85% of 500s trace back to a small set of IID-shard instances (i-az3-{042,043}). Those hosts show elevated memory pressure and increased GC pauses in the runtime.
- Root cause hypothesis (short-term): sudden burst of long-context requests causing KV-cache churn + oversized batches hitting a kernel path that regresses under that mix.

Immediate mitigations applied (now):
1) Reduce max_batch_size for the affected route from 32 -> 8 to reduce latency tail.
2) Pin routing away from i-az3-042/043 and drain connections for rolling reboot.
3) Enable model-variant fallback to the 8-bit quantized variant for new traffic to reduce memory/GC pressure.

I've attached a short CSV with host error counts and a diff of the runtime flags I pushed. Recommend we keep these mitigations for 12-24h while we monitor.

Karthik
Sr Engineering Manager — Serving Runtime
